skill.name: reasoning-counterfactual
skill.description: Evaluate alternative decisions and future scenarios by comparing actual outcomes with probability-weighted counterfactual projections.
skill.summary: Compare actual decisions with plausible alternatives using structured counterfactual reasoning.
skill.author: BellaBe

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to learn from decisions without overfitting to hindsight. This skill structures counterfactual analysis with minimal interventions, probability weights, and clear comparison outputs.
actual_capabilities: Frames an actual decision, observed outcome, and causal chain before comparing alternatives.
Defines a focused intervention that changes one decision variable where possible.
Projects expected, optimistic, and pessimistic alternative outcomes with probabilities.
Compares actual and alternative outcomes across quantitative and qualitative dimensions.
Extracts lessons, recommendations, and future decision implications.
limitations: Counterfactual results depend on the quality of the supplied facts and assumptions.
The skill cannot prove what would have happened in the alternative scenario.
It works best when outcomes can be measured or described clearly.
It does not replace domain expertise for legal, financial, or medical decisions.

use_cases.title: Review a product decision
use_cases.description: Assess whether a launch, pricing, or roadmap choice likely outperformed available alternatives.

use_cases.title: Plan a strategic scenario
use_cases.description: Compare likely outcomes if a competitor, market, or internal constraint changes.

use_cases.title: Learn from past outcomes
use_cases.description: Convert a completed project result into practical lessons for future decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Basic decision review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one past decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use counterfactual reasoning to evaluate this decision: [decision]. Actual outcome: [outcome]. Alternative to test: [alternative].

prompt_templates.title: Compare business options
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze what likely would have changed if we chose [option B] instead of [option A]. Include assumptions, probabilities, and tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a strategic intervention
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with several plausible futures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Model expected, optimistic, and pessimistic outcomes for this intervention: [intervention]. Compare against our current path using probability weights.

prompt_templates.title: Run a multi-intervention retrospective
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these alternatives to our actual decision: [alternatives]. Rank them by outcome quality, confidence, feasibility, and lessons for future action.

output_examples.input: Should we have lowered enterprise pricing before launch?
output: The lower price alternative likely improves sales velocity and deal count.
The expected revenue gain is moderate because each deal is smaller.
Confidence is medium because customer quality and sales behavior remain uncertain.
Recommendation: test a lower entry tier before changing the whole pricing model.

output_examples.input: What if we had accepted funding instead of staying bootstrapped?
output: The funded path likely increases growth speed and hiring capacity.
Ownership dilution reduces part of the financial upside.
The two paths appear similar in expected value but differ in risk profile.
Recommendation: use funding only if growth constraints become the main blocker.

output_examples.input: What if we delayed launch by one quarter to improve quality?
output: The delayed launch likely reduces early support issues and improves retention.
It also postpones customer learning and near-term revenue.
The better choice depends on defect severity and runway pressure.
Recommendation: compare delay cost against the expected churn reduction.

best_practices: State the actual decision, date, context, and observed outcome before testing alternatives.
Change one variable at a time and document assumptions that remain constant.
Use probability weights and confidence levels instead of single certain outcomes.
anti_patterns: Do not judge the past using information that was unavailable at the time.
Do not compare alternatives without explaining the causal chain behind each outcome.
Do not treat speculative projections as proof of what would have happened.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It compares actual outcomes with plausible alternative outcomes to improve decisions and learning.

faq.question: Can it predict the exact alternative outcome?
faq.answer: No. It estimates plausible outcomes with probabilities and clearly stated uncertainty.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the actual decision, timing, context, outcome, metrics, and the alternative you want to test.

faq.question: Does it work for future planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can evaluate hypothetical future interventions when assumptions and success metrics are clear.

faq.question: How is this different from causal reasoning?
faq.answer: Causal reasoning explains why something happened. Counterfactual reasoning compares what happened with plausible alternatives.
